newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling opens unchanged amid tension.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling opens unchanged amid tension.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling opened on a steady note on Friday but the market remained gripped by political jitters a day after the currency slumped to a new official record low.
Commercial banks posted a commercial mean opening of 70.26 against the dollar, unchanged from Thursday's close.

Thursday's drop to a record low meant the shilling has lost 18.08 percent against the dollar since Kenya was jolted by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) halting a $205 million aid package to Kenya a week ago.
Nairobi was calm on Friday morning but many shops and some private offices were closed because of fears of violence coinciding with a one-day national strike called by some opposition leaders.
"The market is still looking very nervous but we are expecting a quiet day because most people and businesses will not turn up," a senior dealer from a leading commercial bank told Reuters on Friday.
But dealers said they were taking no chances and would trade cautiously maintaining wide spreads.
In a bid to calm a turbulent market, Finance minister Musalia Mudavadi said the government was considering talks with the IMF on securing a second year of a loan arrangement.
Mudavadi told Kenyan public and investing community that the government was fully committed to pursuing sound fiscal and monetary policies.
An IMF spokesman said Kenya had to address governance issues before any more talks.
